raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44355.

Adding `--disable-radix-cache` can make a working hybrid attention model failduring cache sizing when speculative decoding is enabled.

If `--max-running-requests` is unset, speculative decoding defaults it to 48. With radix caching disabled, the cache planner treats that default as a user-supplied limit. The saved state and temporary draft state for those requests can consume all the memory left for caches.

Without speculative decoding, the request limit stays unset and the plannerfits the state cache to available memory. It also skips the temporary draft states.

This change uses the existing memory-based sizing path when the automatic state cache exceeds the configured Mamba memory share.

The trigger for this issue depends on the state size and memory budget, not just the model's parameter count.

## Modifications

Track whether the user set `--max-running-requests`, so cache sizing can distinguish an explicit limit from the automatic default. Store this through the existing derived schedule settings. When radix caching is disabled and the automatic state cache would leave no KV memory, use the existing memory-based sizing path.

Explicit request limits and explicit state-cache limits keep their current sizing. Automatic pools keep their current sizing only when they fit within the configured Mamba memory share; larger pools use memory-based sizing to preserve room for the KV cache.

Add a registered CPU test that catches the original failure, with checks for an automatic pool that already fits, explicit request limits (including 48), and an explicit state-cache limit.

## Accuracy Tests

Base: upstream main `3a9cae27edec392ff8cc9f09d1164f557c653f42` using the dependencies required by that commit.

**Reproduction**

- Reproduced the single-flag-change failure with Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 on GB10
  using both native v0.5.21 and unpatched main.
- Qwen passed target-only and speculative/radix-enabled endpoint controls.
- On native v0.5.21, target-only with radix caching disabled and no explicit
  request limit also passed health/model discovery and all eight test chats.
  This completes the comparison of both radix settings with and without
  speculative decoding.
- On native v0.5.21, adding `--max-running-requests 10` to the failing command
  also passed health/model discovery and all eight test chats.
- The bug has also been reproduced with other models that use the same
  state-cache sizing code.

**With the fix**

- Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 on GB10 serves with the previously failing
  command and no explicit request limit. Health and model discovery pass,
  and all eight deterministic test chats return the correct answers.
- GSM8K: 193/200 (96.5%), using four evaluation threads, greedy decoding,
  thinking disabled, and a maximum of 512 output tokens. Mean speculative
  acceptance length: 3.62. This is a small sanity check.

**CPU checks**

- The regression test fails on unpatched main because the state cache leaves a negative KV memory budget. The compatibility checks pass before the fix. All four tests pass with the fix.
- Configuration checks: 35 tests and 31 subtests passed. Coverage of changed lines is 85% against upstream main (100% in cache sizing).
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed

The detailed GPU results reported here cover Qwen3-Next on a single GB10.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark was run. This change fixes startup cache sizing.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

> Adding --disable-radix-cache can make a working hybrid attention model failduring cache sizing when speculative decoding is enabled.

@rystewart-nvidia Why do we add `--disable-radix-cache` flag? This flag should never be added in practice
@YAMY1234 could you review this since this is related to mamba cache + Spec Dec? Thanks
[by Claude Code] Review of the automatic hybrid speculative state-cache sizing fix. Two inline comments below: one sizing cliff near the auto-fit threshold, and one `getattr` cleanup.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`auto_fit_spec_state` turns on only when the default pool needs all of `total_rest_memory`. Just below that point, the 48-slot pool stays and KV gets almost nothing. More memory then gives far less KV.

**Example**

With the new test's Qwen3-Next shapes, `_handle_max_mamba_cache(24.68)` leaves 13.09 GiB for KV, but `24.70` leaves 0.018 GiB. That tiny pool caps `max_req_len` in `tp_worker.py`, or fails `MemoryPoolConfig.__post_init__` if it rounds to zero tokens.

**Fix**

Compare against the auto-fit Mamba share, `total_rest_memory * r / (1 + r)` with `r = mamba_full_memory_ratio`. With that change, the four new tests still pass locally and KV grows with memory. It also shrinks some pools that fit today (30 GiB: 48 to 27 slots), like the radix-enabled path does. Add a 24.70 GiB case.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`max_running_requests_is_explicit_of` adds `getattr(record, "_raw_input", None)`. New defensive `getattr` is not allowed, and this one is not needed. `resolve_once` freezes the record during resolution, and defaults such as the speculative 48 go through `declare_resolution`, not the record. So `record.max_running_requests` already equals `_raw_input["max_running_requests"]`.

**Fix**

```python
def max_running_requests_is_explicit_of(cfg) -> bool:
    from sglang.srt.arg_groups.model_override_base import record_of

    return record_of(cfg).max_running_requests is not None
```

With this change, the new tests and `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` still pass locally.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

All four tests in this file fail on current main. Commit 3edb156dec added a `self.fused_entry_bytes("mamba")` call to `_handle_max_mamba_cache`, and that path reads `self.spec_aux_config`. The bare `object.__new__(KVCacheConfigurator)` planner never sets that slot, so each call raises `AttributeError: 'KVCacheConfigurator' object has no attribute 'spec_aux_config'`. PR CI tests the merge with main, so `base-a-test-cpu` will fail.

**Fix**

Set the fields that `_fused_draft_decision` reads:

```python
planner.spec_aux_config = None
planner.is_hybrid_swa = False
planner.is_draft_worker = False
```

With this change on the PR merged into main `61a676125a`, this file and `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` pass (19 passed), and the sizing results do not change.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`auto_fit_spec_state` turns on only when the default pool needs all of `total_rest_memory`. Just below that point, the 48-slot pool stays and KV gets almost nothing. More memory then gives far less KV.

**Example**

With the new test's Qwen3-Next shapes, `_handle_max_mamba_cache(24.68)` leaves 13.09 GiB for KV, but `24.70` leaves 0.018 GiB. That tiny pool caps `max_req_len` in `tp_worker.py`, or fails `MemoryPoolConfig.__post_init__` if it rounds to zero tokens.

**Fix**

Compare against the auto-fit Mamba share, `total_rest_memory * r / (1 + r)` with `r = mamba_full_memory_ratio`. With that change, the four new tests still pass locally and KV grows with memory. It also shrinks some pools that fit today (30 GiB: 48 to 27 slots), like the radix-enabled path does. Add a 24.70 GiB case.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`max_running_requests_is_explicit_of` adds `getattr(record, "_raw_input", None)`. New defensive `getattr` is not allowed, and this one is not needed. `resolve_once` freezes the record during resolution, and defaults such as the speculative 48 go through `declare_resolution`, not the record. So `record.max_running_requests` already equals `_raw_input["max_running_requests"]`.

**Fix**

```python
def max_running_requests_is_explicit_of(cfg) -> bool:
    from sglang.srt.arg_groups.model_override_base import record_of

    return record_of(cfg).max_running_requests is not None
```

With this change, the new tests and `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` still pass locally.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

All four tests in this file fail on current main. Commit 3edb156dec added a `self.fused_entry_bytes("mamba")` call to `_handle_max_mamba_cache`, and that path reads `self.spec_aux_config`. The bare `object.__new__(KVCacheConfigurator)` planner never sets that slot, so each call raises `AttributeError: 'KVCacheConfigurator' object has no attribute 'spec_aux_config'`. PR CI tests the merge with main, so `base-a-test-cpu` will fail.

**Fix**

Set the fields that `_fused_draft_decision` reads:

```python
planner.spec_aux_config = None
planner.is_hybrid_swa = False
planner.is_draft_worker = False
```

With this change on the PR merged into main `61a676125a`, this file and `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` pass (19 passed), and the sizing results do not change.
